# ghost-killswitch — block all egress except localhost + tunnel reconnect endpoint
# Generated by `airgenome ghost capability engage` (cond.9, operator opt-in).
#
# This anchor is loaded into pf via:
#   sudo pfctl -a ghost-killswitch -f <this-file>
#
# To make persistent across reboots (operator decides):
#   1. copy to /etc/pf.anchors/ghost-killswitch
#   2. add to /etc/pf.conf:
#        anchor "ghost-killswitch"
#        load anchor "ghost-killswitch" from "/etc/pf.anchors/ghost-killswitch"
#   3. sudo pfctl -f /etc/pf.conf
#
# To remove (operator-controlled, no auto-removal — fail-safe is "rules stay"):
#   sudo pfctl -a ghost-killswitch -F all
#
# Variables substituted by capability_engage_kill_switch():
#   __TUNNEL_ENDPOINT__   — Mullvad relay IPv4 (e.g. via `mullvad relay get`)
#   __TUNNEL_PORT__       — WireGuard UDP port (default 51820)
#   __TUNNEL_IFACE__      — utun interface (e.g. utun4) created by Mullvad
#
# Posture: deny-by-default. Only localhost + the single tunnel endpoint
# (UDP, WireGuard) + the tunnel virtual interface itself are allowed out.
# Everything else egresses through the tunnel iface (passes the second
# `pass out quick on __TUNNEL_IFACE__` rule) — kernel guarantees no leak
# to the physical NIC if the tunnel goes down.

# 1. block everything outbound by default
block out all

# 2. localhost is always fine (no leak risk; needed for hexa exec / loopback)
pass out quick on lo0 all

# 3. allow the WireGuard handshake to reach the relay (UDP only, fixed port)
pass out quick proto udp from any to __TUNNEL_ENDPOINT__ port __TUNNEL_PORT__

# 4. allow anything that already has been routed into the tunnel virtual iface
#    — by definition this traffic is encrypted + tunneled, so leak-safe.
pass out quick on __TUNNEL_IFACE__ all
